title: Next — The Dead Mall
summary: Full-page composition: A fog-dark view deeper into the offshore district from the newly reached edge: runner marks on wet concrete, one practical light high inside an unfinished structure, black water threading beneath elevated walkways. Keep the destination suggestive rather than explanatory; no core characters.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — THE DEAD MALL

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They crossed the flats expecting ruins.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: What they found was a district.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That should be enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It isn’t.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There are marks on the walls from people who came before them. Lights inside buildings nobody finished. Dry floors above flooded ones. Routes with names. Rules nobody wrote down.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And somewhere ahead, an abandoned mall has become a place to stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Eat.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Trade stories.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Decide whether the building noise was always there.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The first crossing answered the easy question:

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Tide Town is real.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now they get to find out what happens when a place that should be empty starts feeling occupied.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page teaser image aimed deeper into the district: wet runner marks, incomplete concrete, one distant practical work light and black water under elevated structures. Do not reveal the mall interior or any coming scene. Put NEXT — THE DEAD MALL at top and use fog-dark negative space for the teaser copy, with TIDE TOWN IS REAL as the strongest display beat.

title: Next — No Signal
summary: Full-page composition: Back inland, damp boots and tide gear are already drying beside a repacked bag at an apartment door; charging lights glow while ordinary morning rain falls outside. The image should make another crossing feel disturbingly routine. No people visible.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — NO SIGNAL

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They made it out.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That should reset everything.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Instead, now they know the route back.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know what to pack.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know which lights mean people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They know how long the walk takes when the mud is bad.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And they know when the next low tide is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One crossing can be a story.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Two can be a coincidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: After that, you start making room for it in your life.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Bags stay packed.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Group chats get shorter.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Schedules move.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And a place with no signal starts sounding less like a problem and more like the point.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page teaser still life at an apartment entrance: wet boots, damp rain shell, charged headlamp and bag already repacked for the next tide. Ordinary inland life remains visible beyond. Keep the visual quiet and inevitable, with NEXT — NO SIGNAL at top and the final sentence isolated near the door.

title: Next — Between Runs
summary: Full-page composition: The return route across the flats after repeated crossings, now cut by many overlapping boot tracks instead of a few tentative prints; Harbor Phase glows inland while additional distant headlamps collect near the floodwall. No identifiable core characters.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — BETWEEN RUNS

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The first few trips took planning.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the bags are already by the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not obsession. Not yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Just convenience.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A tide alert instead of a calendar. A late arrival explained with a joke. One more evening offshore because the next window is better. One more story somebody else wishes they had been there for.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Meanwhile the place is changing too.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More runners.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More names.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More attention.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: More people who think they know the rules.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some places do not trap you.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They just give you a reason to keep coming back.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page flats image dominated by layered boot tracks and shallow water, showing that a once-rare route is becoming habitual and social. Harbor Phase practical light glows far inland; anonymous headlamps gather near the threshold. Keep the page atmospheric, with NEXT — BETWEEN RUNS at top and the last two lines separated as the landing beat.

title: Next — Return Tide
summary: Full-page composition: The floodwall ferry lot on the eve of a major run, visibly busier than before: more parked cars, more anonymous gear piles, more practical headlamps and contractor lights, with the low-tide route open beyond. Keep individual runners small and unidentifiable.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — RETURN TIDE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They have routes now.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Reputations.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People who recognize them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A place at the center of something.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And the next tide is going lower than usual.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That should sound like an opportunity.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It does.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There will be more people this time. More cameras. Farther routes. More confidence borrowed from the fact that the last few crossings worked.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Kevin does not like the conditions.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Ryan likes them less.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Everybody else knows what they are doing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Which is usually the moment a bad idea becomes a plan.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page threshold teaser with a crowded but grounded staging lot: anonymous runners, cars, headlamps, cameras and damp gear against the massive floodwall. The exposed route beyond looks enticingly open. Reserve upper fog and wet pavement reflection for copy; land the final line alone near the route entrance.

title: Next — After the Water
summary: Full-page composition: The route has vanished under black returning water beyond the floodwall; the staging area is wet, sparse and stunned, with abandoned temporary lights and blurred phone screens catching the aftermath. No people or identifiable faces.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — AFTER THE WATER

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: By morning, everyone will want a version of what happened.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There will be clips.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Maps.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Arguments.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People who were not there explaining what the people who were there should have done.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Five friends came back across the flats.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: One did not.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For once, nobody in the group has a joke.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The ocean has already covered the route again.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And Tide Town has never looked more interesting to everyone else.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page aftermath teaser from the inland side of the floodwall: black water has erased the walking route, temporary runner lights sit wet and unused, and a few blurred phone screens glow without readable content. Keep the emptiness more important than spectacle. NEXT — AFTER THE WATER sits high; FIVE FRIENDS CAME BACK / ONE DID NOT receives strong typographic separation.

title: Next — The Last Low Tide
summary: Full-page composition: A later low-tide staging area after the crowds have thinned: fewer cars, dark unused runner LEDs, wet concrete, fog, and the route beginning to expose again beyond the wall. The place feels quieter rather than safer. No identifiable characters.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: NEXT — THE LAST LOW TIDE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They got what they said they wanted.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A real place.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Real stakes.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A story nobody could dismiss.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: It cost more than the story was worth.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the crowds are thinning.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The jokes do not land the same.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The old routes feel smaller.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And the name Tide Town sounds like something they made up to avoid saying what it actually was.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the tide drops one more time.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No audience.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No need to prove anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No good reason to go back.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Which leaves the only reason that matters:

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: they still want to see it.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page quiet threshold teaser: the familiar ferry lot is almost empty, runner lights mostly dark, wet concrete and fog leading to a route that is beginning to emerge again. No core cast. Keep NEXT — THE LAST LOW TIDE understated and isolate THEY STILL WANT TO SEE IT as the final page-turn beat.

title: From the Editor
summary: Full-page composition: Dawn over functioning Harbor Phase after the tide has returned, with transit starting, windows lighting, umbrellas appearing and black water held beyond the flood-control system. The city is ordinary, alive and neither triumphant nor broken. Leave pale sky and reflective glass for the final editor note.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Low Tide began with a simple idea:

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: What if the future actually worked?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not perfectly. Not without loss. But well enough that nobody had to become a hero just to survive it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then what?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People still want consequence. Mystery. A place that is not optimized for them. A story they did not inherit from an app, a job, a feed, or a system that already knows what they are likely to choose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The offshore district never needed to be magic.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The tide did not teach anybody a lesson.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The city did not fail.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Six friends went looking for something harder to name, and for a while, they found it together.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The water came back anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY TEXT
dialogueInline.text: Thank you for crossing with them.

source: Low Tide Signal — editorial framing pages
panelPlan: Single full-page dawn Harbor Phase cityscape after the water has returned: transit starting, occupied windows brightening, umbrellas and freight moving, flood-control systems simply working. No core cast. The city should feel alive and ordinary, not like a victory shot. Use pale sky and reflective glass as the copy field and let THANK YOU FOR CROSSING WITH THEM sit alone at the bottom.
